## Why this matters

A shared set of tools means anyone in the lab can find, open and continue anyone else's work. This module is mostly hands-on: by the end, your accounts are set up and connected. All of these tools have good tutorials; if you don't know one, follow the link and spend a few minutes with it.

## Everything lives in the cloud [BA]{.ba-tag}

::: callout-important
## Super important
We **don't use local files**, such as an Excel sheet saved on one specific computer. Everything is in Google Workspace, so it is shared, backed up and version controlled.
:::

- [Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com/) tools: Docs, Drive, Sheets, Forms, Calendar, Meet. They make collaboration easy.
- Pre-registrations are submitted on [OSF Registries](https://osf.io/registries). (We no longer use OSF *projects* for storing files.)
- The lab keeps ready-made [templates]({{< var links.templates >}}) for recurring documents: manuscripts, pre-registrations, participant IDs, scale keys and more. The modules point to the relevant ones.

## Communication and scheduling [BA]{.ba-tag}

- We communicate on [Slack]({{< var links.slack >}}). Rarely, when outside parties are involved, we use MS Teams.
- Meetings and task deadlines are scheduled in [Google Calendar](https://calendar.google.com/). **RSVP to every invite (accept or decline) at least 2 days in advance.**
- Meetings are online in [Google Meet](https://meet.google.com/) by default.
- To find a time for a group meeting, we use [When2meet](https://www.when2meet.com/). You can import your availability from Google Calendar instead of clicking it in by hand.
- For external communication, the lab has a shared email address: {{< var links.lab_email >}}.

## Project management in ClickUp

We use [ClickUp]({{< var links.clickup >}}) to track tasks, who is responsible, dependencies and deadlines.

- Team members share progress and comments on the task itself.
- Task outputs (documents, repositories) are linked from the task, so others can find them.
- It shows bottlenecks early and makes it easier to share or reallocate work.

Your own onboarding is a ClickUp task, too. Each **Do** item in this course is a checklist item there.

## At the university [BA]{.ba-tag}

- Set up [eduroam](https://www.esnelte.hu/wifi-setup-elte) for internet access on campus.
- University software licences are available from the [ELTE IIG site](https://iig.elte.hu/content/szoftver-disztribucio.cl.991?m=5807).

## Reference manager: Zotero [BA]{.ba-tag}

You **must** use a reference manager; handmade reference lists are not acceptable. Learn [Zotero](https://www.zotero.org/): it is free, works with Google Docs, and is what you will use in your own documents. (The lab also has a Paperpile account; you will be told if a project uses it.)

To get going:

- [Zotero quick start guide](https://www.zotero.org/support/quick_start_guide)
- [Using Zotero with Google Docs](https://www.zotero.org/support/google_docs)
- The Zotero Connector browser extension, which saves a paper with one click from the journal's page.

## Generative AI and AI agents [BA]{.ba-tag}

We encourage using AI. Used well, it saves hours on routine work and makes you better at the rest.

- **Chat assistants** such as [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/), [Claude](https://claude.ai/) or [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/) are great for drafting and editing text, explaining statistics, writing and debugging R code, getting feedback, and brainstorming. [DeepL](https://www.deepl.com/) is excellent for translation.
- **AI agents** go further: they work through multi-step tasks on your files and apps on their own. Examples are Claude (with its file and app connectors, or Claude Code), ChatGPT's agent and Codex, and [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot)'s coding agent. Typical lab uses:
  - prefilling a lab template (for example, a pre-registration from the research plan, or scale keys from a questionnaire);
  - writing and running an analysis script, then fixing its errors;
  - turning meeting notes into ClickUp tasks, or tidying up a project folder.

The rules:

- **You are responsible** for everything you submit, whoever or whatever drafted it. Read it, check it, and make sure you understand it.
- **Check the parts that matter most:** references, numbers, statistical claims and code results.
- **Never put non-anonymized participant data or other confidential information into an AI tool.** Give agents access only to the files a task needs.
- Follow the Faculty's [guideline on AI-generated content](https://ppk.elte.hu/en/documents/artificial-intelligence), and disclose AI use where journals or the university require it.

## Do

These tasks are also in your ClickUp onboarding task.

- [ ] Accept the ClickUp invitation and find your onboarding task.
- [ ] Send your Google account address to the lab leader so you can be added to shared folders and calendars.
- [ ] Set up eduroam on your laptop and phone.
- [ ] Zotero training: install Zotero and the Zotero Connector, save three papers from the web, then insert two citations and a bibliography into a new Google Doc.
- [ ] Try an AI assistant on a real task, for example ask it to explain a statistical method you'll need, and check its answer against a textbook or paper.

## Check yourself

::: quiz
You collected pilot data in an Excel file on the lab computer. What should you do with it?

- [ ] Leave it there; everyone in the lab can use that computer.
- [ ] Email it to yourself so you have a copy.
- [x] Move it to the project's shared Google Drive folder (ideally as a Google Sheet).

::: explain
We don't use local files. Data and documents go to the project's shared cloud storage, where they are backed up, version controlled and accessible to the team.
:::
:::

::: quiz
Which reference list is acceptable in a lab manuscript?

- [ ] A carefully typed APA reference list.
- [ ] References copied from Google Scholar's "Cite" button.
- [x] A bibliography generated by Zotero (or the lab's Paperpile).

::: explain
Handmade reference lists aren't accepted, however careful. A reference manager keeps citations and the bibliography consistent and lets us switch citation style with one click.
:::
:::

::: quiz
You want an AI agent to prefill a pre-registration template from your study's documents. Which of these must you **not** give it?

- [ ] The research plan
- [ ] The questionnaire items
- [x] The raw data file with participants' names and emails
- [ ] The lab's pre-registration template

::: explain
Never put non-anonymized participant data or other confidential information into an AI tool. Everything else here is exactly what the agent needs.
:::
:::

::: quiz
You need to find a time for a meeting with five people. What do you use?

- [ ] A long Slack thread
- [x] When2meet
- [ ] Email back and forth

::: explain
We use When2meet for scheduling group meetings, and you can import your Google Calendar availability into it.
:::
:::
